_readme: BSI Customizer sign-in configuration template - the only version of this file
that is committed. For development builds, copy it to auth.json next to the EXE
(or point BSIC_AUTH_FILE at it) and fill it in; never commit the filled-in copy.
Official release builds use the embedded policy and ignore local auth overrides.
When a Discord role gate is configured, it is mandatory on every login:
the current member roles must grant access; allowUsers cannot bypass it.
discord.allowUsers is used only when no role gate is configured.
The role gate uses GET /users/@me/guilds/{guildId}/member, which needs the
guilds.members.read scope (added automatically when a role gate is configured,
so the identify-only scope below is enough).
discord.clientSecret is OPTIONAL for the public PKCE client.
Release builds require it to be empty because secrets in EXEs are extractable.
Configure Discord as a public client, or put confidential token exchange on a server.
The whole file can also be baked into the build from the ZLP_AUTH_JSON secret
(or passed as the ZLP_AUTH_JSON env blob) - see _embed below.
The optional `updater` object below makes the app self-update from a
Discord releases channel (the repository is private, so GitHub Releases
cannot be read by a shipped EXE). See docs/UPDATER.md; leave it empty
and the app simply has no self-updater.

discord_portal: Add a redirect URI in the Discord developer portal that matches exactly:
Scheme, host, port and path all have to match, and 127.0.0.1 is used
instead of localhost on purpose (localhost may resolve to ::1).
_embed: ZLP_AUTH_JSON (repository secret) = this whole auth.json as one blob,
embedded by GitHub Actions. The release workflow requires this secret
and ignores local auth.json / environment overrides for Discord policy.
Development builds without BSI_REQUIRE_EMBEDDED_AUTH accept local config
